Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Coverage and verification procedure:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, their approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps,
and uncertain or occluded regions. These are estimates from this input, not calibration.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. A valid
hierarchy verifies only the parts you emitted; it does not establish image completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible parts because they are small.
For composite objects, match the overall silhouette and the distribution of occupied space
and gaps before adding fine repeated details. Estimate component sizes relative to their
parent and nearby objects from the reference. A correct outer bounding box alone does not
ensure the correct internal density, component proportions or visible coverage. Keep these
parameters explicit so that a later revision can change them without rebuilding the design.

Use the first execution for a complete scene, leaving the second available for correction.
After a successful render, compare the reference inventory against the full rendered view:
missing or extra visible parts, silhouette, internal gaps, relative sizes, overlaps and image
bounds. Identify the largest supported discrepancies before revising. If many objects share
a displacement or scale error, consider camera/framing; if a discrepancy is local, consider
that object's parameters. Neither pattern proves a unique cause. Preserve matching objects
and their editable hierarchy while correcting the supported discrepancies. Do not impose
one fixed density, camera, object count or parameter adjustment across different inputs.
An isolated-object view, if supplied, can clarify membership and silhouette, but its full-image
score is not evidence that removing the rest of the scene improves the reconstruction.
Keep unresolved mappings and occluded geometry explicitly uncertain.

Execution cost planning:
The entire solve has three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds. A short
Python loop can generate thousands of Blender objects before any image exists. Plan a
compact complete first build so that realization and the runner's render can finish with
time for review. Do not change the runner's resource policy or rendering settings to evade
this budget. Use geometry complexity as the controllable cost.
Before returning code, estimate expanded primitive counts in comments, including nested
loops and helper calls. In this implementation, each ball, rod and box emits a separate
mesh and marker; a fillet_box can expand to 26 primitives; sweep_tube with n points emits
2*n-1 primitives. Cloning and layout helpers duplicate their contents. Boolean operands
also incur mesh creation and modifier work. Count these expansions, not just named assets.
Aim initially for a few hundred primitive meshes across the whole scene, as a planning
heuristic rather than a measured runtime guarantee or fixed object count. Allocate detail
according to visible pixel size, silhouette and gaps. If the estimate reaches thousands,
simplify repeated microstructure before execution while retaining every inventory object
and its meaningful editable parts. Represent unresolved surface detail with shared materials
and restrained procedural shading; retain geometric detail that changes visible contours,
openings or occlusions. Avoid nested per-element decoration below the image resolution.
Use short, adaptively spaced tube paths for visible curves, concentrating points at bends.
Avoid many nearly identical Boolean slices to approximate one hollow shape; use a small
number of appropriate SceneAct solids and cutters, preserving the visible opening. Prefer
boxes or scaled balls where their silhouettes suffice; reserve fillet_box for parts whose
rounded edges matter. Keep a small reusable material palette for each surface family rather
than generating a distinct random color and material for every tiny primitive. Keep parent
assets, semantic child parts, and support relations intact during simplification.
If execution times out without an image, report that completion failed and the bottleneck
is unknown unless logs locate it. When a retry remains, reduce expanded primitive counts,
Boolean operations and material proliferation in the complete program. Do not infer camera,
coverage or appearance defects from a timeout. A reduced-cost build still needs execution
and rendered-image verification; simplification alone is not evidence of success.

lighting and materials after realization; do not assume a default world exists. When setting

Before returning code, check API arguments, positive dimensions, noncoincident rod endpoints,
and fillet radii against the smallest dimension. If execution fails, use the actual traceback
to repair the program. A failed execution without an image supplies no rendered visual
feedback: do not treat it as evidence for unrelated camera or geometry changes. Preserve
explicit failures and unknowns; do not claim verification when no successful render exists.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

```python
# Reference inventory and approximate normalized image anchors:
# - Dark carpeted floor: foreground lower half, rear boundary from (0.11, .61)
#   to (.52, .59), extending to both lower corners.
# - Beige back wall: roughly (.11, .37) to (.52, .61); right wall meets it
#   near (.52, .36)-(.52, .59) and fills the right side.
# - Suspended white ceiling: upper portion, with grid edges converging toward
#   the back-right corner. Several dark missing tiles appear at the left edge.
# - Whiteboard: right wall, approximately (.59, .25)-(.91, .58), with a thin
#   gray perimeter and a vertical center division.
# - American flag: hangs near the upper back-right corner, around
#   (.45, .32)-(.51, .42); its support angles toward the right wall.
# - Back wall: dark vent at (.15, .44)-(.24, .47), electrical panel and
#   dangling gray cover around (.30, .46)-(.38, .54), small wall controls.
# - Yellow folded insulation or mat on floor at (.56, .68)-(.90, .80);
#   pale strips continue diagonally toward the lower-right edge.
# - Scattered dark broken ceiling pieces and thin rails occupy the lower-left
#   and middle foreground. Left foreground has a bright partial partition.
# Occluded space beyond the left partition and the exact shapes of debris are
# uncertain. Dominant edges converge toward the rear corner; the right wall
# base slopes downward to the right, while ceiling grid lines recede rearward.
# Primitive estimate: architecture 9, ceiling grid and panels 38, whiteboard 5,
# flag 18, back-wall equipment 10, debris and insulation 24: about 104 meshes.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math

scene = Scene("Abandoned classroom")

# Major dimensions and camera parameters are kept separate for adjustment.
room_width = 6.8
room_depth = 13.0
room_height = 3.2
back_y = 6.5
right_x = room_width / 2
camera_pos = (-2.45, -6.6, 1.65)
camera_target = (0.0, 5.9, 1.70)
camera_lens = 25

wall = (0.68, 0.67, 0.62)
ceiling = (0.72, 0.74, 0.73)
grid = (0.47, 0.49, 0.48)
carpet = (0.105, 0.11, 0.105)
baseboard = (0.085, 0.09, 0.085)
metal = (0.36, 0.38, 0.37)
white = (0.80, 0.82, 0.81)

architecture = Asset("Room architecture")
architecture.include("carpet floor", box((room_width, room_depth, .12),
    center=(0, 0, -.06), color=carpet))
architecture.include("back wall", box((room_width, .12, room_height),
    center=(0, back_y, room_height/2), color=wall))
architecture.include("right wall", box((.12, room_depth, room_height),
    center=(right_x, 0, room_height/2), color=(.72, .71, .67)))
architecture.include("back baseboard", box((room_width, .035, .14),
    center=(0, back_y-.08, .09), color=baseboard))
architecture.include("right baseboard", box((.035, room_depth, .14),
    center=(right_x-.08, 0, .09), color=baseboard))
# Bright partition cropped by the left edge of the photograph.
architecture.include("left partition", box((.10, 4.1, 2.45),
    center=(-3.25, -3.15, 1.23), color=(.84,.86,.85)))
architecture.include("partition vertical seam", box((.018,.025,2.36),
    center=(-3.19,-1.85,1.22), color=(.68,.70,.69)))
scene.include("architecture", architecture)

# Ceiling plane with a regular suspended grid. Dark openings along the left
# edge represent missing tiles.
roof = Asset("Suspended ceiling")
roof.include("ceiling surface", box((room_width, room_depth, .08),
    center=(0, 0, room_height+.04), color=ceiling))
for i in range(8):
    x = -3.35 + i * .95
    roof.include("long grid %02d" % i,
        box((.025, room_depth, .022), center=(x,0,room_height-.015), color=grid))
for i in range(14):
    y = -6.3 + i * .95
    roof.include("cross grid %02d" % i,
        box((room_width,.025,.022), center=(0,y,room_height-.017), color=grid))
for i, y in enumerate((-3.9,-2.0,-.1,1.8)):
    roof.include("missing tile %d" % i,
        box((.55,.65,.025), center=(-3.0,y,room_height-.025), color=(.12,.15,.15)))
# A few light ceiling panels and a smoke detector.
for i, y in enumerate((-2.8, .1, 3.0)):
    roof.include("light panel %d" % i,
        box((.83,.83,.018), center=(-1.95,y,room_height-.03), color=(.86,.87,.84)))
roof.include("smoke detector", ball(.10, center=(-2.0,-4.15,room_height-.055),
                                    color=(.79,.80,.77)))
scene.include("ceiling", roof)

board = Asset("Wall mounted whiteboard")
board_y = 2.85
board_z = 1.91
board_length = 3.35
board_height = 1.38
board.include("white writing surface", box((.035,board_length,board_height),
    center=(right_x-.085,board_y,board_z), color=(.85,.87,.87)))
for z in (board_z-board_height/2, board_z+board_height/2):
    board.include("horizontal frame %.2f" % z,
        box((.045,board_length+.06,.035), center=(right_x-.11,board_y,z), color=metal))
for y in (board_y-board_length/2, board_y+board_length/2):
    board.include("end frame %.2f" % y,
        box((.045,.035,board_height), center=(right_x-.11,y,board_z), color=metal))
board.include("center seam", box((.046,.012,board_height),
    center=(right_x-.112,board_y,board_z), color=(.68,.71,.71)))
scene.include("whiteboard", board)

equipment = Asset("Back wall fixtures")
equipment.include("vent", box((.70,.035,.32), center=(-1.92,back_y-.08,1.97),
    color=(.28,.31,.31)))
equipment.include("electrical recess", box((.30,.035,.41),
    center=(-.48,back_y-.08,1.72), color=(.24,.27,.26)))
equipment.include("recess inset", box((.17,.04,.31),
    center=(-.48,back_y-.105,1.72), color=(.51,.54,.51)))
equipment.include("dark switch", box((.06,.045,.10),
    center=(-.49,back_y-.13,1.75), color=(.12,.14,.13)))
cover = box((.40,.035,.36), center=(-.30,back_y-.18,1.46), color=(.47,.50,.48))
cover.turn(axis="+y", degrees=-37)
equipment.include("hanging panel cover", cover)
for i, x in enumerate((.02,.18,.31)):
    equipment.include("small control %d" % i, box((.09,.025,.15),
        center=(x,back_y-.075,1.53), color=(.78,.79,.75)))
scene.include("back wall fixtures", equipment)

flag = Asset("Hanging American flag")
# Flat cloth on the back wall, with stripes and a blue canton.
flag_x = .72
flag_top = 3.03
flag_w = .32
flag_h = .70
flag.include("cloth", box((flag_w,.025,flag_h),
    center=(flag_x,back_y-.18,flag_top-flag_h/2), color=(.83,.82,.77)))
for i in range(7):
    z = flag_top - (i*2+.5)*flag_h/13
    flag.include("red stripe %d" % i, box((flag_w,.012,flag_h/13),
        center=(flag_x,back_y-.198,z), color=(.57,.12,.13)))
flag.include("blue canton", box((flag_w*.45,.015,flag_h*.40),
    center=(flag_x-flag_w*.275,back_y-.209,flag_top-flag_h*.20),
    color=(.12,.18,.31)))
flag.include("flag pole", rod(.018, start=(flag_x-.18,back_y-.20,flag_top+.04),
    end=(flag_x+.23,back_y-.20,flag_top-.16), color=(.32,.31,.29)))
flag.include("angled support", rod(.012, start=(flag_x+.15,back_y-.15,flag_top-.10),
    end=(right_x-.10,5.25,2.86), color=(.20,.20,.18)))
scene.include("flag", flag)

# Broken panels and metal rails on the carpet. Each is an editable part.
debris = Asset("Scattered floor debris")
def flat_piece(name, center, size, angle, color):
    p = box(size, center=center, color=color)
    p.turn(axis="+z", degrees=angle)
    debris.include(name, p)

flat_piece("foreground dark panel", (-1.45,-3.30,.025), (1.48,.56,.035), -10, (.17,.18,.17))
flat_piece("foreground light fragment", (-1.42,-3.23,.052), (.89,.28,.012), -8, (.33,.34,.31))
flat_piece("foreground black slat", (-.82,-3.45,.065), (1.22,.035,.025), 20, (.13,.14,.13))
flat_piece("left dark panel", (-2.5,-1.95,.025), (1.08,.47,.032), -8, (.19,.20,.19))
flat_piece("left gray inset", (-2.47,-1.95,.05), (.74,.20,.012), -8, (.36,.37,.34))
flat_piece("back dark panel", (-1.65,.02,.025), (1.0,.35,.035), 9, (.16,.17,.16))
flat_piece("back light edge", (-1.64,.02,.05), (.73,.045,.012), 9, (.41,.42,.39))
flat_piece("long white rail", (-1.1,-2.32,.045), (1.68,.055,.035), -10, (.69,.72,.70))
flat_piece("small black fragment", (.50,.45,.025), (.42,.19,.025), 18, (.19,.20,.18))
flat_piece("pale small fragment", (1.30,.05,.03), (.35,.22,.025), -17, (.56,.55,.47))
scene.include("floor debris", debris)

insulation = Asset("Yellow insulation and floor strips")
# The slightly overlapping slabs make the folded, low pile.
flat_piece_dummy = None
for i in range(3):
    slab = box((1.65,.65,.055), center=(1.92, -1.07-i*.24, .06+i*.028),
               color=(.72+i*.025,.62+i*.025,.30+i*.02))
    slab.turn(axis="+z", degrees=-8+i*3)
    insulation.include("folded yellow layer %d" % i, slab)
insulation.include("yellow edge", box((1.28,.12,.045),
    center=(2.03,-1.63,.09), color=(.80,.69,.35)))
for i in range(3):
    strip = box((.11,2.8,.025), center=(2.65+i*.23,-3.28,.025),
                color=(.70,.67,.59))
    strip.turn(axis="+z", degrees=22)
    insulation.include("long floor strip %d" % i, strip)
scene.include("insulation and strips", insulation)

realize(scene)

sc = bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("SceneWorld")
sc.world.use_nodes = True
background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get("Background")
if background is None:
    background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBackground")
output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get("World Output")
if output is None:
    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputWorld")
sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs["Background"], output.inputs["Surface"])
background.inputs["Color"].default_value = (0.65, 0.68, 0.69, 1)
background.inputs["Strength"].default_value = 0.65

set_view(camera_pos, camera_target, lens=camera_lens, sensor=36)
area_emitter((-2.6,-3.3,3.0), power=420, size=4.0,
             target=(0,2,1.2), color=(.90,.94,1.0))
area_emitter((0,3.0,3.0), power=260, size=3.0,
             target=(0,2,0), color=(1.0,.96,.88))
```
